clue.text: They're small and very trying on the feet!

definitions.text: They're small and very trying on the feet!

parts.words: They're small and very trying on the feet!
parts.note: little children who are a trial to their parents, and who are also trying out walking, unsteady on their feet

explanation.definitionFit: Children just learning to walk are tiny, exhausting for parents, and attempting to stay upright.

clue.text: Named flier set the pace

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, something that flies
led means went in front and set the pace

explanation.surface: A named bird that led the flock.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a title such as Lord means being given a rank by name.

clue.text: Second string for the principal violinist?

definitions.text: Second string for the principal violinist?

parts.words: Second string for the principal violinist?
parts.note: the orchestra's first violinist has a name for the role, and the stand-in is the second string in that role

explanation.walkthrough: 'Second string' means a substitute, though it hints at a violin's strings.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchestra's first violinist is called the leader in Britain, and the substitute for that player is the second in command.

clue.text: See 2
Could be about vitality, albeit theoretical

definitions.note: the definition is an adjective; the answer is a theory, the noun

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: the letters of the next word could be arranged into something else

explanation.surface: A hypothesis about life force, though only on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' signals the anagram of the word after it. 'albeit theoretical' points to Einstein's famous theory rather than to any adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Einstein's famous work is a theory, so the clue calls it by that quality.

clue.text: Capital in credit on the Norfolk coast

indicators.note: the capital city is placed inside the abbreviation for credit

parts.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Money raised for a capital project, deposited somewhere along the Norfolk coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: CROMER is a seaside town on the north Norfolk coast, in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is a resort sited on that county's shoreline, so the location phrase describes it.

clue.text: Colleague in space

parts.note: a companion sharing the same space, meaning the same room, rather than outer space

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shares your bedroom or lodgings is a companion in that shared space.

clue.text: Navigational point of 18

parts.note: 18 is the drawing force between iron and a lodestone; the compass pointer works by it

explanation.walkthrough: Entry 18 is ATTRACTION, here in the sense of magnetic pull.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass pointer swings north by magnetic pull, the attraction of entry 18.

clue.text: Hold tenure about a couple of seconds and give a further appointment

indicators.note: the word for holding tenure is put about, around, the other letters

parts.note: to reign is to hold office as a monarch
two of S, the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: An official who holds a post briefly and is then posted again.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint someone again or to another post is to allocate them anew.

clue.text: Privileged place aboard well above the salt

definitions.text: Privileged place aboard well above the salt

parts.words: Privileged place aboard well above the salt
parts.note: at old banquets the salt cellar divided honoured guests from lesser ones; the most honoured sat at the board furthest from it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Aboard' is read as 'at the board' (the dining table), not on a ship; sitting 'above the salt' meant sitting among the distinguished guests.
explanation.definitionFit: At a formal dinner the honoured guests sit at the head board, the seat of distinction.

clue.text: Lucretia recalling first-class leading tennis player

parts.note: Bjorn Borg, Swedish champion who led the men's game around 1980

indicators.note: calling back suggests the grading for first-class is read from its end

parts.note: A1 is the classic mark of top quality, written here as AI

explanation.surface: Someone named Lucretia remembering a top-ranked tennis star of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalling' signals the backwards reading of the first-class mark. Lucretia Borgia was the notorious Renaissance noblewoman, daughter of Pope Alexander VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucretia Borgia is the famous Italian noblewoman of that family, so her first name points to the surname.

clue.text: Makes a request in earnest to leave nothing

indicators.note: being 'in earnest' is read as the letters set into a new order, a working of that word
to leave the zero means it is dropped from the little word before it

parts.note: nothing is zero, the round letter O

explanation.surface: Someone pleads seriously for permission to go away with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave nothing' takes O out of TO, giving T; EARNEST plus T, rearranged as signalled by 'in', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to beg or plead, which is asking for something earnestly.

clue.text: City to find one's bearing in a second

indicators.note: the word for bearing is put inside the short pair of letters for a second

parts.note: one's mien is one's bearing or manner

explanation.surface: A traveller trying to get oriented in a city in a single moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' suggests a compass direction but means demeanour here. AMIENS is a city in northern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiens is a cathedral city in Picardy, northern France.

clue.text: Mighty hunter's run -or is it a hold-up?

definitions.text: Mighty hunter's run -or is it a hold-up?

parts.words: Mighty hunter's run -or is it a hold-up?
parts.note: the great hunter of the night sky has a row of three stars across his middle, like a strap that keeps trousers up

explanation.walkthrough: Orion is the mighty hunter of Greek myth; 'run' hints at belting along, and a belt is what holds trousers up.
explanation.definitionFit: The row of three stars in the constellation of the hunter is pictured as the strap round his waist.

clue.text: Extremely slender, for example, that's about all

indicators.note: the abbreviation for 'for example' goes round the other words

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation of the Latin for 'for example'
very is a synonym of extremely
thin means slender

explanation.surface: A very thin example seems to sum up the whole situation.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun for every single thing is the whole of something, the totality.

clue.text: Musical ensemble past it, and wound up?

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
aged means old, past one's best

explanation.surface: An old pop group now too old to perform, and finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound up' reads as finished, but it means a wound wrapped up in dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressed injury has been wrapped in strips of gauze, bound up.

clue.text: Keep one's distance in Rugby

definitions.meaning: to remain aloof, apart from others
a rugby union position, the half-back who links scrum half and three-quarters

explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is a town and school in England where the sport began, but here it is the game itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back and remain aloof is one phrase; the fly-half position in rugby union is another name for the same words.

clue.text: Fair entertainment with bird at the back of a vehicle

indicators.note: the bird is placed behind the vehicle, so the vehicle comes first

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
an ousel (ouzel) is a blackbird or the ring ouzel

explanation.surface: A fairground ride where a bird perches on the rear of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: A carousel is a merry-go-round at a fair; 'fair' is the funfair, not just.
explanation.definitionFit: A merry-go-round is a classic ride at a funfair.

clue.text: Inducement at drawing

parts.note: traction is the act of drawing or pulling something along

explanation.surface: An incentive offered at a sketching session.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that draws people in is a lure or incentive.

clue.text: See 7
I fill a sort of role befitting one's child

indicators.note: a sort of signals the preceding letters made into some different form

explanation.surface: A parent filling a role suited to a son or daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of' rearranges I FILL A; 'role' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes duty or love owed by a son or daughter to a parent.

clue.text: Highballs for slipshod enthusiasts?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, balls hit very high into the air
keen sportspeople whose footwear is made for slipping over snow

explanation.walkthrough: 'Highballs' looks like whisky drinks but means steepling cricket hits.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a skied hit soars high; people on skis are shod for sliding downhill.

clue.text: French revolutionary black-belt heavyweight

parts.note: a dan is a grade of black belt in judo and karate
a ton is a very heavy weight

explanation.surface: A revolutionary in France who was also a martial artist and a hefty fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: Georges Danton was a leader of the French Revolution, guillotined in 1794.
explanation.definitionFit: Danton was one of the chief figures of the 1789 uprising in France.

clue.text: Star to note

parts.note: a little star-shaped printed mark sends the reader to a footnote

explanation.definitionFit: The printed symbol shaped like a star flags text and points to a footnote.

clue.text: Bird for King George on the river

indicators.note: one piece placed directly against the other in the order the clue gives

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
the Ouse is the name of several English rivers

explanation.surface: A game bird shot for the king beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: GR appears on postboxes from George V's and George VI's reigns; the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire and another in East Anglia.
explanation.definitionFit: The red grouse is a game bird of moorland.

clue.text: Wrinkle from the ambassador in Deal resort

parts.note: an ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE

indicators.note: to re-sort the letters is to arrange them again

explanation.surface: The ambassador picks up a wrinkle while staying at Deal, a Kent seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town, Deal being a Kent seaside town, but read as re-sort it rearranges IN DEAL to ADLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A crease across the forehead is a line on one's head, as a wrinkle is.

clue.text: Spoil a gorge

definitions.meaning: to spoil here means to sully or make unclean
a narrow valley or passage through which troops march in single file

explanation.definitionFit: To spoil is to pollute or desecrate; a gorge is a narrow pass between steep slopes.

clue.text: Jack's aspiring objectives

parts.note: 'Jack' is the tail of the word for a worker who climbs high church towers, and the towers point upwards, aspiring

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Jack' as the end of steeplejack, the man who climbs church spires; 'aspiring' means rising upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall pointed church towers are what such a high-climbing repairer aims for, and they rise skyward.
